context_requirements: Expression of SQLE and an intact sterol regulatory element-binding protein (SREBP) pathway
Active cholesterol biosynthesis and dependence on the mevalonate pathway
Cellular capacity to sense sterol depletion and upregulate SREBP target genes
falsifiers: No consistent upregulation of SREBP target genes (e.g., HMGCR, HMGCS1, SQLE) at 6 or 24 hours in any cell line
Lack of dose-dependent transcriptional response across the nine cell lines
Predominant downregulation of cholesterol biosynthesis genes instead of compensatory upregulation

changes: Removed SQLE from the falsifier example list because SQLE itself is not among the 978 landmark genes and cannot be measured in this experiment.

Kept HMGCR, HMGCS1, FDFT1, EBP, NSDHL, INSIG1, and ACAT2 in the up lists: inhibiting SQLE depletes sterols and relieves SREBP inhibition, so these SREBP targets are expected to be transcriptionally upregulated.
Kept proximal_down and late_down empty: no landmark gene is expected to be directly downregulated by SQLE inhibition at the transcriptional level.
Kept kinetics as slow and magnitude as weak at 6 h and moderate at 24 h: transcriptional compensation through SREBP requires protein synthesis and is typically delayed.
Kept HEPG2 as moderate and all other lines as weak: hepatocyte-like cells have high basal sterol biosynthesis and SREBP activity, while the other lines are less dependent on the mevalonate pathway.
Kept generic_effects as none: the listed genes are specific sterol-pathway/SREBP targets rather than generic proliferation or stress genes.
Kept evidence empty: no citations were provided, so none could be verified against abstracts.
